title: Park a mobile robot workcell on its feet
instruction: Press the two leveling pedals so the front wheels clear the worktop. Leave the robot base parked on its feet.
context: Mobile robot workcells roll between jobs and rest on fixed supports while operating. Deploying the two front feet keeps the loaded station steady before the robot is run.
setup: A folded, secured 8.0 kg industrial arm on a 430 × 390 × 6 mm aluminum deck weighs 10.72 kg with the deck. The rear feet and the front two 50 × 25 mm wheels support it at reset. Each front caster has an independent 32 mm support pad 1.2 mm above the worktop. Its steel eccentric cam is operated by a 41 × 40 × 14 mm rectangular pedal grip. The starting layout and part coordinates are in the README.
scoring: With hands clear, award 0.25 for one front pad touching the surface with its wheel at least 2 mm above it. Award 0.5 when both corners meet that condition and 1.0 when they hold for 0.5 s. The deck must stay within 6 mm of its starting position. Lifting, holding or blocking the base to create clearance, leaving the parking area or tipping more than 15° earns zero.
reset_notes: Raise the pedals. Restore the deck to the start position with both front wheels touching and the two front pads 1.2 mm clear. Reset velocities, joints, counters and camera buffers.
fidelity: Physical eccentric cams contact the two separate pad followers. Each pad takes load from its wheel and the cam travels beyond center to hold the released state. The cart is a compact mobile lab fixture carrying a fixed robot. Cam geometry, bearing drag and pad compliance are modeling estimates.
